completable-future-basics.title: CompletableFuture basics
completable-future-basics.why: Methods such as thenApply describe what happens after completion, letting dependencies between asynchronous stages be assembled as values.
completable-future-basics.tips: Model exceptional completion with exceptionally, handle, or related methods. Choose execution resources according to whether work is CPU-bound or I/O-bound.

switch-expression-yield.title: Switch expressions and yield
switch-expression-yield.short: Produce a value directly from branching
switch-expression-yield.summary: Use switch as an expression that returns a value.
switch-expression-yield.why: A switch expression keeps the value produced by each branch in one expression instead of repeatedly assigning a variable.
switch-expression-yield.tips: Use yield when a case needs multiple statements before producing its value. Some switch subjects require exhaustive cases.

collectors-grouping-by.title: Group stream elements by key
collectors-grouping-by.summary: Collect elements into a Map keyed by a classifier.
collectors-grouping-by.why: groupingBy expresses the common initialize-a-map-and-append-to-lists pattern as a stream reduction.
collectors-grouping-by.tips: A downstream collector can count or transform each group at the same time. Consider the size of the resulting structure for large inputs.

files-walk-tree.title: Walk a directory tree recursively
files-walk-tree.summary: Traverse a directory tree as a Stream of Path values.
files-walk-tree.why: Files.walk lazily exposes paths below a starting directory and composes naturally with stream operations such as filter.
files-walk-tree.tips: Close the returned Stream with try-with-resources. Decide explicitly how symbolic links should be handled for the application.

date-time-parse-exception.title: Date text does not match its format
date-time-parse-exception.why: LocalDate.parse expects ISO date text by default, so other field orders or separators require a matching formatter.
date-time-parse-exception.tips: Treat parse failure as normal for external input and keep the accepted input format and formatter definition together.

stream-reuse-illegal-state.title: A consumed Stream cannot be reused
stream-reuse-illegal-state.short: A terminal operation already consumed the stream
stream-reuse-illegal-state.summary: Treat a Stream as a single-use processing pipeline.
stream-reuse-illegal-state.why: After a terminal operation such as count or findFirst, the stream is consumed; operating on the same stream again can throw IllegalStateException.
stream-reuse-illegal-state.tips: When multiple traversals are needed, create a fresh stream from the original Collection or other reusable source each time.

illegal-forward-reference.title: Illegal forward reference
illegal-forward-reference.short: A field initializer refers to a later field too early
illegal-forward-reference.summary: Order field declarations so simple-name references are valid during initialization.
illegal-forward-reference.why: Java restricts some forward references in field initializers because initialization proceeds in declaration order and a simple name can otherwise read a field before its declaration is reached.
illegal-forward-reference.tips: Move the depended-on field earlier or restructure initialization instead of relying on declaration-order tricks.

ambiguous-overload-null.title: null makes an overloaded call ambiguous
ambiguous-overload-null.why: When unrelated reference types are overloaded, null can match each of them and the compiler may have no single most-specific method to select.
ambiguous-overload-null.tips: A cast can state the intended type, but first consider whether the ambiguous overload design itself can be avoided.

raw-type-usage-warning.title: Raw type usage warning
raw-type-usage-warning.short: A generic type was used without type arguments
raw-type-usage-warning.summary: Prefer parameterized types such as List<String>.
raw-type-usage-warning.why: Raw types remain for compatibility with older Java code, but weaken element-type checking and can move type errors to runtime.
raw-type-usage-warning.tips: Specify type arguments except at unavoidable legacy boundaries; use forms such as List<?> when the element type is unknown.

stringbuilder-equals-identity.title: StringBuilder.equals does not compare contents
stringbuilder-equals-identity.short: Equal text in different builders does not imply equality
stringbuilder-equals-identity.summary: Compare StringBuilder contents through text-aware operations.
stringbuilder-equals-identity.why: StringBuilder does not override equals for content equality, so equals effectively tests whether the references identify the same object.
stringbuilder-equals-identity.tips: Use toString or contentEquals for textual comparison and avoid treating StringBuilder itself as a value object.
